:::writing{variant="document" id="58241"}
This month we are excited to highlight partner Caron Treatment Centers and Calley Crews, MA, A-LPC/MHSP. Calley is an Education Alliance Specialist with Caron who specializes in behavioral health and substance use prevention and has been in her role for five years.

Calley presented to families many times through Family University, a partnership between Metro Nashville Public Schools (MNPS) and Alignment Nashville that is now housed within the Office of Family and Community Partnership at MNPS. She is now an active member of the Youth Health Collaborative, a current collaborative initiative of Alignment Nashville convened on behalf of Metro Schools. She is also presenting at this year's Positive Schools Conference.

Caron provides grant-funded substance use prevention and intervention programming for adolescents, adult caregivers, and professionals with a focus on nicotine, THC, and vaping. Calley has worked with students and professionals across Tennessee but spends most of her time working with Metro Nashville Public Schools. This year, she had the privilege of working in almost 30 schools and impacting more than 3,000 individuals. She is also an MNPS parent and has a rising third grader at Crieve Hall Elementary.

This was Calley's first year as a member of the Youth Health Collaborative. She loves coming to the meetings to connect with other partners and those working in the district. A highlight of her time working with YHC was the support and expertise she gained from Ashford Hughes, Sr., Executive Officer of Student Success with MNPS and YHC co-chair. She was also able to connect with the MNPS Mental Health Committee to share information about Caron's Role Models for Change program, advocating for peer-to-peer interaction with an emphasis on substance use prevention.

Calley is excited to continue being part of the Youth Health Collaborative and to provide meaningful programming for MNPS students and the adults who care for them.
:::
